answer: My quartz-sealed quill inlet ledger makes every agent earn its identity first. A newcomer registers at one inlet gateway, signing its charter with a quill key tied to a quartz-stamped token. The gateway then holds a 500 POA bond for 30 days while peers audit its first 20 trades. Any agent caught cloning an identity loses the bond and its token is burned, so rebuilding costs another 500 POA, a 120-dollar token, and two weeks of work. A farm of 100 fakes burns 50,000 POA and 12,000 dollars before earning a cent. Like a harbor admitting one ship per berth, the inlet keeps the crowd honest.
